Class add_or_edit_inventory

java.lang.Object
controller.add_or_edit_inventory
All Implemented Interfaces:
javafx.fxml.Initializable
public class add_or_edit_inventory extends Object implements javafx.fxml.Initializable
Inventory Add and Edit Page.

Controls the manager inventory editing page and the operations performed on inventory records. The page displays current inventory information and supports adding items, editing item details, restocking quantities, recording stock counts, and deleting inventory items.

Quantity-changing operations are also recorded in the inventory history table so inventory changes can be tracked over time. This controller also manages field states, status messages, database transactions, and navigation between manager and employee pages.

    • initialize

      public void initialize(URL location, ResourceBundle resources)
      Initializes the inventory editing page when the FXML view is loaded.

      The inventory table is configured and populated from the database, and all editing fields begin disabled. A table-selection listener displays the selected inventory record in the fields on the right side of the page.

      Specified by:
      initialize in interface javafx.fxml.Initializable
      Parameters:
      location - location used by JavaFX to resolve relative resources
      resources - resource bundle supplied by JavaFX during initialization

    • setManagerUsername

      public void setManagerUsername(String username)

      The stored username is passed to other controllers when navigating between manager pages or entering employee mode.

      Parameters:
      username - username of the currently logged-in manager

    • setupTable

      private void setupTable()
      Configures the inventory table columns and maps each column to the matching value stored in an inventory row.

      The displayed values include supply ID, item name, quantity, ordering units, cost, most recent change type, and recorded time.

    • loadInventory

      private void loadInventory()
      Loads the current inventory records from the database into the table.

      Each database row is converted into a map containing the values expected by the table columns. A missing recorded timestamp is displayed as an empty value. Records are ordered by supply ID.

      If the database query fails, the exception is printed and an error message is displayed on the page.

    • displaySelectedItem

      private void displaySelectedItem(Map row)
      Displays the selected inventory record in the editing fields.

      The selected supply ID and original quantity are stored for later edit, restock, stock-count, or delete operations. Selecting a row does not automatically start an editing mode, so the fields remain disabled until an action is chosen.

      Parameters:
      row - selected inventory row from the table

    • getSelectedRow

      private Map getSelectedRow()
      Returns the inventory row currently selected in the table.

      The selected supply ID and original quantity are also stored for later database operations. If no row is selected, an error message is displayed.

      Returns:
      selected inventory row, or null when no row is selected

    • handleAdd

      private void handleAdd()
      Starts the process of adding a new inventory item.

      Any existing table selection is cleared, the current item state is reset, and all inventory input fields are enabled. The controller enters add_or_edit_inventory.Mode.ADD so Save Changes will create a new database record.

    • handleEdit

      private void handleEdit()
      Prepares the selected inventory item for editing.

      Item name, ordering units, and cost become editable while quantity remains disabled. Quantity changes are handled separately through Restock or Stock Count so quantity history remains accurate.

    • handleRestock

      private void handleRestock()
      Prepares the selected inventory item for a restock operation.

      Only the quantity field is enabled. The field is cleared so the entered value represents the amount being added rather than the final quantity. The controller enters add_or_edit_inventory.Mode.RESTOCK.

    • handleStockCount

      private void handleStockCount()
      Prepares the selected inventory item for a physical stock-count update.

      Only the quantity field is enabled. The entered value represents the actual quantity currently counted in stock, and the difference from the previously stored quantity is recorded in inventory history.

    • handleSave

      private void handleSave()
      Saves the operation represented by the current inventory mode.

      Add, edit, restock, and stock-count actions are sent to their matching save methods. If no action has been selected, an error message is displayed instead of changing the database.

    • saveAdd

      private void saveAdd()
      Validates the input fields and saves a new inventory item.

      Name, units, cost, and quantity are required. Cost and quantity are checked for valid nonnegative numeric values. A new supply ID is then calculated and both the inventory record and its initial history record are inserted within the same database transaction.

      The transaction is committed only after both inserts succeed. Any failure rolls the transaction back so the inventory and history tables remain consistent.

    • getNextSupplyId

      private int getNextSupplyId(Connection conn) throws SQLException
      Finds the next available supply ID in the inventory table.

      The next ID is calculated as one greater than the current maximum supply ID. If the inventory table is empty, the method returns 1.

      Parameters:
      conn - active database connection used to query the inventory table
      Returns:
      next available supply ID
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the database query cannot be completed

    • saveEdit

      private void saveEdit()
      Validates and saves changes to the selected inventory item's details.

      The item name, ordering units, and cost are updated while quantity is left unchanged. The inventory row is marked as an edited item and a matching history record is inserted with a quantity change of zero.

      Both database operations are performed in one transaction. A failure causes the transaction to roll back.

    • saveRestock

      private void saveRestock()
      Validates and saves a restock quantity change.

      The entered quantity must be a positive whole number. It is added to the quantity that was stored when the item was selected, and the resulting total is saved through updateQuantity(int, int, String, String).

    • saveStockCount

      private void saveStockCount()
      Validates and saves a physical stock count for the selected item.

      The entered value must be a nonnegative whole number. The difference between the actual count and the previously stored quantity is calculated so both the new quantity and its change can be recorded.

    • updateQuantity

      private void updateQuantity(int newQty, int quantityChange, String changeType, String successMessage)
      Updates an inventory quantity and records the same change in inventory history.

      The inventory table receives the new quantity, change type, and current timestamp. A matching inventory-history row stores the quantity change, resulting quantity, change type, and timestamp. Both operations use one transaction so they either succeed together or are rolled back together.

      Parameters:
      newQty - final quantity that should be stored in inventory
      quantityChange - amount added, removed, or corrected
      changeType - description of the inventory change being recorded
      successMessage - message displayed after a successful transaction

    • handleDelete

      private void handleDelete()
      Deletes the selected inventory item after confirmation.

      A confirmation dialog displays the selected item name before deletion. If confirmed, a deletion history record is created with the current quantity removed and a resulting quantity of zero. The inventory row is then deleted in the same transaction.

      If either database operation fails, the transaction is rolled back and an error message is displayed.

    • disableAllFields

      private void disableAllFields()
      Disables all inventory input fields.

      This state is used when no add, edit, restock, or stock-count operation is currently active.

    • setFieldStates

      private void setFieldStates(boolean disableName, boolean disableUnits, boolean disableCost, boolean disableQty)
      Sets the enabled or disabled state of each inventory input field.

      Different inventory modes use different combinations of editable fields. For example, editing allows name, units, and cost while restocking and stock counting allow only quantity.

      Parameters:
      disableName - true to disable the item name field
      disableUnits - true to disable the ordering units field
      disableCost - true to disable the cost field
      disableQty - true to disable the quantity field

    • clearFields

      private void clearFields()
      Clears all inventory input fields on the right side of the page.

      The table contents are not changed by this method.

    • value

      private String value(Object object)
      Converts an object from an inventory row into displayable text.

      Null database values are converted to an empty string so the text fields can be updated without a null value.

      Parameters:

      Returns:
      empty string for null, otherwise the object's string value

    • finishSuccessfulOperation

      private void finishSuccessfulOperation(String message)
      Resets the page after an inventory operation completes successfully.

      The inventory table is reloaded, the table selection and input fields are cleared, all fields are disabled, and the controller returns to add_or_edit_inventory.Mode.NONE. The supplied success message is then displayed.

      Parameters:
      message - success message displayed after the page is reset
